newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper ends down on LME losses.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper ends down on LME losses.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended down sharply on Wednesday, with most contracts breaching the key 19,000-yuan support level due to overnight losses on the kerb market of the London Metal Exchange, traders said.
The most active February 1997 contract ended at an intra- day low of 18,790, down 390 yuan. It opened at a high of 19,020.
November fell 310 to 18,550 yuan, December 280 to 18,600, January 320 to 18,780, March 290 to 18,910, April 200 to 19,000 and May 200 to 19,050.
Combined volume rose to 66,090 tonnes from 63,880.
Copper opened lower and traded mostly at intra-day highs and fell further before closing at intra-day lows.
Traders said long liquidation and fresh short-selling triggered by LME losses pushed prices steadily down.
"Short position holders took advantage of LME losses to build short positions at high levels while long position holders were eager to offset theirs," one trader said.
"Weak market sentiment made few investors want to build long positions at the current level," he added.
Traders said copper was still consolidating between $1,900 and $1,970 on the LME despite successive sharp drops of copper stockpiles, which should be positive for LME prices.
"Investors are wary of a drop in LME stockpiles because China's domestic consumption has not improved obviously in October which is usually a boom month," a second trader said.
Aluminium ended down. November fell 180 to 13,200 yuan per tonne and December and January fell 200 to 13,000.
Combined volume fell to 1,210 tonnes from 1,350.
